QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_13

question.text: The NAV of a Cat III open-ended AIF scheme must be calculated and disclosed to investors at a minimum frequency of:

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the CTR disclosure on NAV, for Cat III OPEN-ENDED schemes the NAV must be disclosed to investors at MONTHLY intervals (close-ended Cat III funds disclose quarterly). Many Cat III hedge-fund-style AIFs compute NAV daily internally, but the disclosure regulatory floor is monthly for open-ended. **The Trap:** Daily is operational norm but not the regulatory disclosure floor. Weekly is a made-up middle ground. Quarterly is the rule for CLOSE-ENDED Cat III. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B tests client-facing NAV cadence. XIX-C/D test NAV regulation across all categories. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Even if the regulatory floor is monthly, publish daily dealing NAV to LPs — it tightens discipline on marks (listed equities must be marked intraday) and helps side-pocket triggers be identified early.
